name: Zachary McVicker
headline: Sports medicine orthopedic surgeon, hip arthroscopy and preservation
location: West Palm Beach and Jupiter, FL
on_the_show: Dr. McVicker explained femoroacetabular impingement, the hip problem that often shows up as back or groin pain. He described the two forms, the cam lesion where the ball is misshapen and the pincer lesion where the socket covers too much of it, and said pincer lesions are the harder of the two to treat. He compared the labrum to a gasket that keeps a suction seal and spreads weight across the joint, and said that arthroscopic surgery is minimally invasive and keeps your own hip, along with the balance and proprioception a replacement cannot give back.
on_the_show_quote: Instead of being round, it’s more like an oval peg in a round hole.

background.text: He earned his medical degree at the University of Toledo College of Medicine and Life Sciences and completed his orthopedic surgery training at the University of Rochester Medical Center.

He completed a sports medicine fellowship at the Cedars-Sinai Kerlan-Jobe Institute in Los Angeles, serving as an assistant team physician for teams including the Los Angeles Rams, Los Angeles Dodgers and USC football.
Since moving to Jupiter he has served as an assistant team physician for the Miami Marlins and the Jupiter Hammerheads and as team physician for Jupiter Christian High School.

He has a special interest in hip injuries, including femoroacetabular impingement, labral tears, hip dysplasia, and gluteus medius and hamstring injuries, and is trained in hip arthroscopy and cartilage restoration.
He sees patients at the Paley Institute offices in West Palm Beach and Jupiter.

research_notes: Identity confirmed: Paley Institute sports medicine surgeon in West Palm Beach and Jupiter with a hip focus, Kerlan-Jobe fellowship, matching the episode. His own practice page writes his name Zachary; he goes by Zach on air. On air he said he joined Paley from Dr. Frank Cook's former practice in 2022 ('I believe'); the Paley page says he has served the Jupiter community since 2020, which is consistent but I left the join date out of background. The Episode 10 blurb says he is board certified by the American Board of Orthopaedic Surgery, but the Paley page does not state board certification, so I did not include it as a web fact. Paley's page bio also carries a stray 'Oxbridge Academy team' phrase that reads as a page error; ignored. The Paley profile's social block also includes a YouTube playlist that is not clearly his alone; omitted. Phone 561-844-5255 is the Paley West Palm Beach number, given on air several times.
